children: Temasek-backed Xora-led round comes as Hang Ten rapidly expands enterprise AI engagements with global companies including Aramco and Siemens Gamesa

AI services startup Hang Ten Systems founded by former Infosys CEO Vishal Sikka, has raised an additional USD 53 million in seed funding led by Xora, a Temasek-backed investment firm, taking its total funding to USD 85 million, the company said on Thursday.
Mayfield, which led Hang Ten's first seed round, and Aramco Ventures also participated in the latest round. The company did not disclose its valuation.
The two seed rounds were completed five weeks apart, as Hang Ten moved rapidly from fundraising to securing multi-million-dollar contracts with global enterprises, the company said.

The company said it has signed several contracts spanning advisory and software development work, with projects ranging from short-term consulting assignments to multi-year development programmes. Some projects are already being delivered, while others have been completed.

Hang Ten provides advisory, transformation and applied-AI services to large enterprises. Its delivery model combines agentic code generation, a reusable library of AI-enabled skills and domain expertise to build, modify and operate enterprise software.
The company said its approach is aimed at reducing the cost and time required for enterprise software implementation compared with traditional systems integration models.

The new funding will be used to expand delivery capacity for projects already underway, grow its engineering and consulting teams and develop its platform, infrastructure and library of agentic skills, it said.

"Enterprise technology has long been one of the largest cost lines in essential industries," said Phil Inagaki, managing partner and chief investment officer at Xora. He said the challenge for enterprises was not simply adopting AI but implementing it securely and economically at scale.
Hang Ten is already working with Saudi Aramco on applications across several business functions, while Siemens Gamesa Renewable Energy is also among its enterprise customers.

Mahdi Aladel, CEO of Aramco Ventures, said the breadth of Hang Ten's approach had led Aramco teams to identify multiple potential AI applications across its operations, with projects already being scoped.

Siemens Gamesa CEO Vinod Philip said the company began working with Hang Ten two months ago on a limited set of outcomes and subsequently expanded the engagement after the startup delivered what was expected in terms of speed and quality.

Hang Ten was founded by Sikka, who previously served as CEO of SAP from 2014 to 2019. The company's investor base also includes Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan, Micron Technology chairman and CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, and Yahoo co-founder and AME Cloud Ventures founding partner Jerry Yang.
Yang has joined Hang Ten's board of directors.
Sikka said the company's focus was on applying AI to critical enterprise systems while maintaining reliability.
"AI can be the most powerful amplifier we have ever built," Sikka said. "But in the enterprise, AI's power must go hand-in-hand with reliability."
